newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

District quota system for entering university to be abolished from August 1999, says M.D.D. Peiris, Secretary, Ministry of Education. Students who get required marks will have to sit an aptitude test instead, he said.

Sri Lankans in UK launch campaign to counter LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) disinformation being dished out by groups working for the rebels, says the International Foundation of Sri Lankans.
National carrier Airlanka raises airfares by three percent from January 1, mainly due to rising prices of aviation fuel, airline sources say.
Police detect 18 kilograms of heroin from a house in a town north of Colombo. Take into custody a Pakistani national and his Sri Lankan girlfriend.
Government schools reopen for the new year after Christmas holidays.
Troops on "Operation Rivijaya" to clear rebel bases in east advance on three fronts, killing at least 20 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam.
